alterations.description: But most of India’s four hundred and sixty million people see neither pomp nor progress. They still spend their Jives in half a million villages like this — hungry, poor and illiterate. Implements remain as primitive as their way of life, scarcely scratching the worn-out soil. But it remains about the lowest in the world. .... Ancient wells like this are still the only way of getting water Although they are still a rare sight in the Indian countryside. But for most of India's peasantry, the commonplaces of modern society remain a dream. Apathy is partly to blame, so is suspicion of new-fangled ways. Clinics may offer new health to the children, yet their elders retain a deep-seated fear of accepting anything from the doctors and technicians who come flooding in from a remote and mysterious machine called government.
